text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"A binding wage floor above the market equilibrium reduces the amount of labour employers demand.","cited_pids":["min_wage#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Teen and low-skill employment fell in several regions after sharp minimum wage increases relative to neighbouring areas.","cited_pids":["min_wage#3"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Low-margin employers may accelerate automation in response to higher minimum wages, cutting entry-level positions.","cited_pids":["min_wage#2"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Hours reductions for low-wage workers after large local minimum wage increases can shrink their earnings gains.","cited_pids":["min_wage#1"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"The Card and Krueger fast food study found no employment decline in New Jersey compared with neighbouring states after its minimum wage increase.","cited_pids":["min_wage#4"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"In monopsony models, where employers have wage-setting power, a moderate minimum wage can raise both wages and employment.","cited_pids":["min_wage#5"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"A meta-analysis of minimum wage studies finds employment effects clustered near zero, with publication bias inflating negative findings.","cited_pids":["min_wage#6"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"Lower worker turnover after a minimum wage increase may leave overall headcount broadly unchanged.","cited_pids":["min_wage#7"]},{"cid":"c9","text":"Employment effects of minimum wage increases depend on the size of the increase and on market structure.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c10","text":"Small or moderate minimum wage increases show little or no job loss in several studies.","cited_pids":[]}]}
